content: WidgetsBindingObserver.didChangeAppLifecycleState reports resumed/inactive/paused/detached/hidden, but also fires for embedded Activity/ViewController transitions unrelated to true backgrounding (e.g. a permission dialog or FaceID prompt triggers inactive/resumed). On iOS/Android, work started in paused/detached callbacks has only a few hundred ms before the OS can suspend or kill the process -- there is no guarantee of completion, and a hard kill (task swipe, OOM) delivers no lifecycle callback at all. Common pitfalls: forgetting to removeObserver in dispose, doing heavy/async work in 'inactive', and assuming a Timer or a recording continues running while backed onto a paused state.
